name: Monthly sales and operations planning cycle for one business unit of a manufacturer
summary: Sales and operations planning (S&OP) is the monthly cycle in which a manufacturer agrees one plan for what it expects to sell and what it will make, buy and hold in stock over the next 12 to 18 months. Demand planners start from last month's sales and a statistical forecast, sales and marketing adjust it, supply planners test it against plant and supplier capacity, finance prices the gaps and a pre-meeting of managers prepares decisions for an executive meeting chaired by the business unit head. The work is spread across six or more departments and moves on a fixed meeting calendar, so most elapsed time is waiting for the next meeting. It is slowed by spreadsheet consolidation, late or biased sales inputs, master data errors and decisions deferred by busy executives.

baseline.org_archetype: A business unit of about 1,200 people with two plants and annual revenue of roughly $400 million, part of a multi-division manufacturer, planning 15 to 25 product families with an ERP, a statistical forecasting module and spreadsheets.
baseline.notes: Describes a formal but not advanced S&OP process (stage two or three of common maturity models): a fixed monthly calendar of reviews exists, but much of the data work is in spreadsheets.

unit_of_work: one monthly S&OP cycle for one business unit
trigger: The calendar month closes and the sales and shipment cut-off is reached (Day 0).
end_state: The executive-approved operating plan is loaded into the master production schedule and the financial latest estimate, and minutes with owners and deadlines are sent out.

volume.seasonality: One cycle every month. Some companies run a lighter cycle in the budget month or in August and December, and add a deeper review once a quarter.

evidence.note: S&OP is run monthly per business unit (src5, src6).

triggered_by.from: Month-end sales and shipment close (order to cash)
triggered_by.object: actual orders, shipments and inventory for the month

produces.to: Master production scheduling and material requirements planning

produces.object: approved demand plan and allocation rules
S&OP minutes, KPI scorecard and decision log

evidence.note: Two demand planners spend roughly 15% of their month on the S&OP cycle itself. Median wage $37.03 (Logisticians, the closest SOC for planners). Loaded cost is the BLS May 2021 median hourly wage times 1.7: 1.50 for benefits (manufacturing compensation over wages, BLS ECEC December 2021) and about 1.13 for overhead such as space, IT and supervision (author estimate).

About 10 to 15 account managers each spend one to two hours a month on forecast input. Median wage $29.61. Loaded cost is the BLS May 2021 median hourly wage times 1.7: 1.50 for benefits (manufacturing compensation over wages, BLS ECEC December 2021) and about 1.13 for overhead such as space, IT and supervision (author estimate).

Loaded cost is the BLS May 2021 median hourly wage times 1.7: 1.50 for benefits (manufacturing compensation over wages, BLS ECEC December 2021) and about 1.13 for overhead such as space, IT and supervision (author estimate).

Prices the demand plan and scenarios. Median wage $44.03. Loaded cost is the BLS May 2021 median hourly wage times 1.7: 1.50 for benefits (manufacturing compensation over wages, BLS ECEC December 2021) and about 1.13 for overhead such as space, IT and supervision (author estimate).

Two supply planners, one of whom keeps the master production schedule. Median wage $37.03. Loaded cost is the BLS May 2021 median hourly wage times 1.7: 1.50 for benefits (manufacturing compensation over wages, BLS ECEC December 2021) and about 1.13 for overhead such as space, IT and supervision (author estimate).

Buyers for the few constrained materials. Median wage $30.51 (Buyers and Purchasing Agents). Loaded cost is the BLS May 2021 median hourly wage times 1.7: 1.50 for benefits (manufacturing compensation over wages, BLS ECEC December 2021) and about 1.13 for overhead such as space, IT and supervision (author estimate).

systems.name: ERP (orders, shipments, inventory, master production schedule)
Statistical forecasting and demand planning module
Supply planning and rough-cut capacity module (or MRP run)

steps.name: Extract month-end history
steps.description: After the sales and shipment cut-off for the month, scheduled jobs pull orders, shipments, returns and inventory by item, customer and location from the ERP into the forecasting module and a staging spreadsheet. Nobody touches it unless the job fails.

error.defect_description: Extract job fails or misses late-posted shipments, leaving gaps in history.

evidence.note: Data gathering after month end is the first S&OP step (src5); src3 sets a Day 0 data cut. Wait of one to three days for the month-end sales cut-off and overnight jobs is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Score last month's forecast
steps.description: The demand planner compares last month's shipments with the forecast made one to three months earlier, calculates forecast error and bias by product family and customer group, and updates the KPI scorecard used in the reviews. Large misses are flagged for discussion.

error.defect_description: Wrong lag or unit of measure used, so accuracy looks better or worse than it is.

evidence.note: Tracking forecast error and bias is part of the reviews (src5) and the KPI dashboard (src3). Hours are the author's estimate for one business unit with 15 to 25 families.

steps.name: Cleanse history and planning master data
steps.description: The demand planner corrects outliers such as one-off orders or stock-outs, links new items to the items they replace, retires discontinued items and fixes customer and family mappings. Most of this is done by exporting to a spreadsheet, editing and loading back.

error.defect_description: Wrong mapping of a new item or an uncorrected outlier distorts the statistical forecast.

evidence.note: History cleansing, master data updates and replacement-item links are described in src5; spreadsheet dependence is reported by 81.1% of src10 respondents. Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run statistical forecast
steps.description: The forecasting module refits its time-series models overnight on the cleansed history and produces a baseline forecast by item, customer group and month for the next 18 months, plus an exception list of items whose forecast moved sharply.

error.defect_description: None introduced by the run itself.

evidence.note: Statistical models are finalised in data gathering (src5); the horizon of 12 to 18 months is from src6. The overnight batch timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review forecast exceptions and tune models
steps.description: The demand planner works through the exception list, checks the largest families against the scorecard and market notes, overrides models that picked the wrong pattern and decides whether a data problem needs another cleansing pass and rerun.

error.defect_description: An override is keyed against the wrong item or month.

next.condition: data problem found, history must be fixed and the model rerun

evidence.note: Exception review is standard demand-planning practice; the 10% rerun rate and hours are the author's estimate from planner practice in mid-size manufacturers.

steps.name: Enter launch, promotion and phase-out assumptions
steps.description: The product manager opens the input template and adds volumes for new product launches, planned promotions or price changes, and the run-down of products being phased out, with a short note on each assumption.

error.defect_description: Launch volumes are optimistic or the launch date has already slipped.

evidence.note: Product review inputs (launches, transitions, retirements) are described in src4 and src7; src6 gives a worked example of promotion and discontinuation adjustments. Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit customer forecast adjustments
steps.description: Each key account manager downloads the template for their customers, compares the baseline with order books, customer forecasts and pipeline, and types adjusted volumes by family and month. The time shown is the total for all account managers in the business unit.

error.defect_description: Inputs are biased upward to secure supply or downward to beat a quota, or entered in the wrong unit.

next.condition: all inputs received by the deadline
some inputs missing at the deadline

evidence.note: Sales and marketing intelligence is merged into the unconstrained consensus forecast (src5). The 40% late-input share and total hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase late sales inputs
steps.description: The demand planner checks which account managers have not returned their templates, sends reminders and copies the sales director when the deadline has passed. If a reply does not come, the planner prepares to carry the previous month's numbers forward.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Chasing late inputs is a common planner task; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send late forecast inputs
steps.description: Account managers who missed the deadline fill in their templates, often quickly and with less checking, and email them to the planner. For any who still do not reply, the planner keeps last month's values.

error.defect_description: Rushed inputs copy last month or miss known changes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the delay and effort for late submitters.

steps.name: Consolidate inputs into draft consensus forecast
steps.description: The demand planner copies the sales and marketing spreadsheets into the forecasting module or a master workbook, reconciles units and families, checks that totals still tie to the baseline plus adjustments and lists the largest changes from last month.

error.defect_description: A row is pasted twice or into the wrong month, inflating demand.

evidence.note: Consolidation into one unconstrained consensus view (src5) is mostly done in spreadsheets (src10). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare demand review pack
steps.description: The demand planner builds the slides for the demand review: consensus versus statistical forecast, versus last month and versus budget by family, the scorecard, the assumptions behind large changes and the open questions for sales.

error.defect_description: Charts built from a stale version of the workbook.

evidence.note: Review dashboards with forecast units, revenue and variance from the last cycle are described in src3. Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold demand review and sign off consensus demand
steps.description: The director of sales chairs a meeting of sales, marketing, product management, demand planning and finance that walks through the families with the largest changes, challenges assumptions and agrees one unconstrained demand plan. The time shown is total attendee time, about eight people for 90 minutes plus preparation.

error.defect_description: Optimism or politics carried into the agreed plan without evidence.

control.basis: Company S&OP policy: sales leadership signs off the consensus demand plan before supply planning starts

next.condition: numbers sent back for revision before sign-off

evidence.note: Demand review chaired by sales with planners, marketing and finance, 90 minutes (src3); sales executives authorise the forecast (src5). The 15% send-back rate and attendee count are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Publish consensus demand to supply planning
steps.description: The demand planner applies the changes agreed in the meeting, locks the consensus version in the forecasting module and releases it to the supply planning module, then emails the minutes and the list of changes.

error.defect_description: A change agreed in the meeting is not keyed.

evidence.note: Publishing the forecast to execution systems and minutes after sign-off are described in src5. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Price the demand plan against budget
steps.description: The financial planning analyst converts the consensus units into revenue and margin using standard prices and costs, compares the result with the annual budget and the last forecast, and notes the gaps that the reconciliation will need to explain.

error.defect_description: Outdated prices or mix assumptions misstate revenue.

evidence.note: The forecast is built in units and translated into dollars (src5, src6). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run rough-cut capacity and supply plan
steps.description: The supply planning module, or an MRP run in the ERP, nets the released demand against inventory and open orders and loads the resulting production by family onto key work centres and critical materials for the next 18 months, producing load reports.

error.defect_description: Stale routings or capacities in master data give a wrong load picture.

evidence.note: Rough-cut capacity and constrained or unconstrained simulations are the core of supply planning (src5, src6). Batch timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Analyse capacity loads and inventory projections
steps.description: The supply planner compares loads with available capacity by work centre and month, checks projected inventory against safety stock and targets, and lists the months and families where demand cannot be met on straight time or where inventory will build.

error.defect_description: A constraint is missed because a work centre's capacity in the system is out of date.

evidence.note: Supply review converts demand into resource requirements and documents gaps (src6). Hours are the author's estimate for two plants.

steps.name: Ask key suppliers to confirm capacity
steps.description: The buyer emails the suppliers of the few constrained materials with the volumes for the coming months and asks them to confirm capacity and lead times, attaching the relevant part of the forecast.

error.defect_description: Forecast quantities sent in the wrong unit or for the wrong months.

evidence.note: Supply review considers material constraints with procurement (src4). Effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for supplier confirmations
steps.description: Suppliers reply by email or phone with what they can supply, sometimes only after a follow-up call. Unanswered requests are treated as unconfirmed and carried as risks into the supply review.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Supplier response time of one to five days is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review labour, shift and overtime options
steps.description: The plant operations manager looks at the load report for the plant, works out what extra shifts, overtime, temporary labour or moving work between lines would cost and what it would deliver, and sends the options to the supply planner.

error.defect_description: Option costs omit training time or overtime limits in the labour agreement.

evidence.note: Mitigation options such as overtime, outsourcing and allocation are outputs of supply review (src4, src6). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft constrained supply plan and scenarios
steps.description: The supply planner turns the gaps, supplier replies and plant options into a constrained supply plan and one or two alternatives, for example build ahead in spring or add a weekend shift, with their effect on service and inventory.

error.defect_description: Scenario uses unconfirmed supplier capacity as if it were firm.

evidence.note: Feasible supply and inventory plans for each scenario are the output of supply review (src4, src5). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold supply review
steps.description: The director of supply chain and operations chairs a meeting with plant managers, supply planning and procurement that agrees the feasible supply plan, ranks the constraints and decides which options need finance pricing or executive decision. The time shown is total attendee time.

error.defect_description: Constraint accepted without checking the data behind it.

control.basis: Company S&OP policy: operations signs off a feasible supply plan before reconciliation

evidence.note: Supply gate led by supply chain planning with operations and procurement, 90 minutes, completed around Day 12 (src3); manufacturing managers approve the supply plan (src5). The 15% rework rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile demand, supply and finance
steps.description: The S&OP manager lines up the consensus demand, the agreed supply plan and the budget, works out where revenue, service or inventory targets will be missed, and frames each gap as a decision with two or three options and an owner.

error.defect_description: Demand and supply versions do not match because one was updated after the review.

evidence.note: Pre-S&OP reconciles demand and supply options into one recommended plan with financial implications (src4, src6); src3 places the financial reconciliation draft around Day 18. Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Price the scenarios
steps.description: The financial planning analyst calculates revenue, margin, inventory value, overtime and freight cost for each option and compares them with the budget and the latest estimate, so the meeting sees the money behind each choice.

error.defect_description: Cost rates out of date or inventory carrying cost left out.

evidence.note: Finance owns the reconciliation gate and shows P&L and cash implications (src3, src4). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold pre-S&OP meeting
steps.description: The S&OP manager runs a meeting of the functional managers from sales, marketing, operations, procurement and finance that settles the issues within their authority, agrees the recommended plan and decides what goes to the executives. The time shown is total attendee time, about eight managers for two hours.

error.defect_description: A decision is escalated without enough data to decide.

next.condition: more analysis needed before the executive meeting

evidence.note: Pre-S&OP attendees and outputs are described in src5 and src6; src3 sets a two-hour reconciliation gate. The 20% rework rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare executive pack
steps.description: The S&OP manager condenses the reconciliation into a short executive pack: KPIs, the recommended plan in units and dollars, the decisions needed with options and the risks, and emails it as a pre-read a day or two before the meeting.

error.defect_description: Numbers in the pack differ from the workbook after late edits.

evidence.note: The executive meeting reviews KPIs, open pre-S&OP issues and financial implications in units and dollars (src5). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Executive S&OP meeting approves the plan
steps.description: The business unit president chairs a meeting of the functional heads that reviews performance, decides the escalated trade-offs such as overtime, build-ahead inventory or customer allocation, and approves one operating plan. The time shown is total attendee time.

error.defect_description: Decision taken on a misread chart.

control.basis: S&OP charter and delegation of authority: the business unit president approves the operating plan and spending on overtime, build-ahead inventory and capacity

next.condition: one or more decisions deferred for more work

evidence.note: Executive meeting chaired by the president or CEO, capped at about one hour, sign-off around Day 22 (src3, src5). Waiting for a slot in executive calendars and the 15% deferral rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close deferred decisions by email
steps.description: The S&OP manager gathers the extra analysis the executives asked for, sends a short note with a recommendation and chases each executive until the decision is confirmed by email or in a short call.

error.defect_description: Decision recorded differently from what an executive meant.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for spending decisions

evidence.note: Deferred decisions closed outside the meeting are common; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Publish minutes and decision log
steps.description: The S&OP manager writes up the decisions, owners and deadlines, updates the action log and sends the minutes and the approved plan to all participants and to the teams who execute it.

error.defect_description: An action is assigned without an owner.

evidence.note: Minutes must be published after each meeting because approved plans drive master scheduling and MRP (src5). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load approved plan into master schedule
steps.description: The supply planner updates the master production schedule in the ERP to match the approved family volumes, breaking families into items for the near months and respecting the frozen period, then reruns MRP so purchasing and the plants see the new plan.

error.defect_description: Quantities keyed into the wrong period or item.

control.basis: Master scheduling policy: changes inside the frozen time fence need master scheduler and plant approval

evidence.note: The approved plan authorises master scheduling, with mix handled below the family level (src5, src6). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the financial forecast
steps.description: The financial planning analyst copies the approved volumes, prices and costs into the finance forecast model so the monthly latest estimate sent to the corporate office matches the operating plan.

error.defect_description: Finance keeps its own volume assumption for some families, so the two plans drift apart.

next.condition: plan released to execution and finance

evidence.note: The approved plan is the authorisation that financial forecasting must follow (src6). Hours are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Late sales inputs
exceptions.description: Some account managers miss the deadline; the planner chases them and either receives rushed inputs or carries last month's values forward.

exceptions.name: Data problem in the statistical forecast
exceptions.description: A mapping or history error is found during exception review, so history is cleansed again and the model rerun.

exceptions.name: Demand numbers sent back
exceptions.description: The demand review does not accept the draft and the planner revises it before sign-off.

exceptions.name: Supply scenario rerun
exceptions.description: The supply review asks for another scenario, for example a different build-ahead profile, before agreeing the plan.

exceptions.name: Extra analysis before the executives
exceptions.description: The pre-meeting cannot agree a recommendation and asks for more analysis and a second short call.

exceptions.name: Executive decision deferred
exceptions.description: The executive meeting defers a trade-off, for example a capacity investment, and it is closed by email days later.

exceptions.name: Executive meeting moved
exceptions.description: Travel or a board meeting pushes the executive meeting back several days, delaying plan release.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the month-end data cut to executive sign-off; the simulated cycle also includes one to two days of release work after sign-off
benchmarks.population: Typical monthly S&OP calendar described by a consulting playbook

evidence.note: src3 places executive sign-off at Day 22 after a Day 0 data cut. The p90 of 28 days is the author's estimate for months where the executive meeting slips or decisions are deferred.

benchmarks.population: APQC Open Standards Benchmarking participants, all industries

evidence.note: Covers all demand and supply planning, not only the S&OP meetings.

benchmarks.unit: extra planning FTEs per 1 billion USD revenue for bottom versus top performers

evidence.note: Shows how widely planning staffing varies.

benchmarks.population: 2012 practitioner survey of demand planners; older than the reference period

evidence.note: Level and lag not stated; treat as a rough order of magnitude.

benchmarks.population: One make-to-stock consumer packaged goods company, MIT thesis

evidence.note: Single case; shows the size of gain from better data treatment and S&OP practice.

benchmarks.population: 164 S&OP and IBP professionals in 54 countries, self-selected online survey (published 2025)

evidence.note: Published after the reference period, but spreadsheet use was at least as common in 2019 to 2022.

benchmarks.population: Recommended cadence in a consulting playbook

evidence.note: A recommended design rather than a measured average; many executive meetings run 90 to 120 minutes.

pain_points.description: Planners spend much of the first week exporting, cleansing and pasting data between the ERP, the forecasting module and spreadsheets, leaving little time for analysis.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet use reported by 81.1% of S&OP practitioners (src10); data gathering is a full step in src5.

pain_points.description: Sales inputs arrive late and carry bias from quotas or fear of shortages, so the consensus forecast is often less accurate than the statistical baseline for some families.

evidence.note: Common practitioner observation; no source opened measured it for this file.

pain_points.description: The supply review and reconciliation get compressed into the second half of the month, so scenarios are few and finance pricing is rushed.

evidence.note: Follows from the fixed calendar in src3, but the compression itself is the author's judgment.

pain_points.description: Executive meetings slip or defer decisions, which delays the plan reaching the master schedule by days.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of how often executive calendars and deferrals delay release.

pain_points.description: The approved plan is re-keyed into the ERP and the finance model by hand, so execution and finance can drift from what was agreed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on common ERP and spreadsheet set-ups of the period.

assumptions: One case is one monthly cycle for one business unit, so cases_per_month is 1 and the staffing check compares stated FTEs with the hands-on hours of a single cycle.

Meeting steps record total attendee minutes under the chair's role, so labour cost for those steps is priced at the chair's rate and slightly overstates cost. The validator adds those attendee minutes to elapsed time, which overstates elapsed time by a few hours per meeting; in the other direction, long analysis steps take several working days of elapsed time that the waits only partly capture.
Meeting dates are fixed in an annual calendar. In reality rework loops are often absorbed before the fixed next meeting, so the simulated rework adds more elapsed time than it does in practice.

The validator adds hands-on minutes to elapsed time, so wait_before_min holds only the idle gap between steps; the two together reproduce a calendar in which the demand review falls around Day 7, the supply review around Day 13, the pre-meeting around Day 19 and the executive meeting around Day 22 to 25.
Parallel work (sales and marketing inputs, supplier confirmations and plant options, finance pricing and capacity runs) is listed in sequence with short waits and named in concurrent_with.
Loaded hourly cost is the BLS May 2021 national median wage for the closest SOC code times 1.7 (1.50 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for manufacturing, about 1.13 overhead by author estimate).
Error probabilities, rework rates and most hours are tier C estimates for a mid-size business unit; the sources describe the steps and calendar but rarely measure effort.
